conviction_note: First print after the 11 Sep 2026 ISEMBYLD approval, covering about three weeks of launch. The evidence is balanced, so p_up is 49 on an abs_move of 12 (implied 11.2%, last first-of-news prints +24% and +10%) and the scaled number is about -0.2. impact_sum (+1.35) leans slightly positive on positioning and a director's buy, but the scaled number lands near zero. The difference is deliberate: the 15% five-day run-up with no cause I could find, and 28 vol points of put skew, pull p_up toward 50, while the crowded short and the low company-set expectations ('steady and consistent new patient starts over time') keep it from going below that.
bar: Disputed and thin, so every finding is capped small. EPS: -$0.86 consensus (Earnings Whispers, https://www.earningswhispers.com/stocks/srrk; Q2 actual -$0.84). Q3 revenue consensus about $0.6M (Benzinga snapshot 2026-10-13, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/SRRK/earnings-forecasts); an earlier Benzinga snapshot said $70k. Q4 consensus $5.2M. Visible Alpha FY2026 $5.3M and FY2027 $133M (S&P Global, 2026-09-23, https://www.spglobal.com/market-intelligence/en/news-insights/research/2026/09/scholar-rock-s-isembyld-approval-sets-up-rapid-sales-ramp, snippet only, page returned 403). There is no company revenue guide. The company's only framing is 'steady and consistent new patient starts over time' (8-K Ex 99.2, 2026-09-14). No source carries a consensus for patient starts or patients on therapy, and that is the line the stock is likely to trade on.
positioning_check: Short interest is crowded. 22.18M shares short as of the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 12.7 days to cover on 1.74M average daily volume. 22.72M short and 9.3 days to cover as of 2026-09-30. Both from https://massive.com/quote/srrk, snapshot of 2026-11-05. Shares outstanding are 121.79M, so about 18% of shares outstanding and more of the float. The trend has been rising since 18.2M on 2026-08-14 (curvedtrading, FINRA basis). Skew: 25-delta put minus call is +27.98 vol points (downside paid). Option OI is only 1,917 contracts and the ATM spread is 55% of mid, so the skew is indicative only. Run-up: +15.07% over 5 days and +17.73% over 20; $39.90 on 2026-10-16 (AAII) and $45.50 on 2026-11-05 (massive) before the sealed $49.375 spot.

findings.finding: Director Srinivas Akkaraju (Samsara BioCapital funds) bought 289,470 SRRK shares in the open market (code P) on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-26 at weighted-average prices of $41.31-41.82, about $12.0M. Samsara's two funds now hold about 7.1M shares. This is the only insider buy in the past year; the CSO sold about $7.9M between December 2025 and February 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior director open-market purchase found to compare against. The stock rose from about $41.5 at the purchase to $49.375 sealed, and some of that move may already reflect the signal.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the Form 4 has been public since 27 October and the stock is up about 19% from the purchase price. What is not priced is the information content. A director with board-level visibility into early launch metrics (enrollment forms, payer approvals) added $12M about two weeks before the first launch print. If the market had fully weighed that, the put skew would not sit at +28 vol points.
findings.independence: Same fact also appears on https://massive.com/quote/srrk (insider table). There is no independent corroboration of what the director knows.

findings.finding: Short interest is crowded into the first launch print: 22.18M shares short at the 2026-10-15 settlement, about 12.7 days to cover and about 18% of the 121.79M shares outstanding. It was 18.2M on 2026-08-14 and 22.72M on 2026-09-30, so it has stayed high through approval. An early-launch number above a near-zero bar gives shorts a reason to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 2025 print (2025-11-14), which carried positive FDA-meeting news, moved +24.41%. The Q2 2026 print (2026-08-06) moved +9.96%. Both were positive surprises into elevated short interest.
findings.why_not_priced: Short interest is a stock of positioning rather than a flow, and its effect is conditional on the print. With days to cover around 12.7, covering on any good launch number cannot happen in one session, which makes the upside tail asymmetric. The put skew suggests options traders price the downside tail more heavily, which is inconsistent with a crowded short the market has fully discounted.
findings.independence: https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/srrk/short-interest/ gives 18.2M shares short and 19.8 days to cover at the 2026-08-14 settlement (FINRA basis). Equibles gives 14.5% of float on 2026-08-20. Different dates, same picture.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar is near zero: about $0.6M consensus (Benzinga, 13 Oct; an earlier snapshot said $70k), against a launch that began 11 Sep with a $11,659 vial list price (about $310k a year per patient) and about 6,600 eligible US patients on SMN2 therapy. The company's own framing was 'steady and consistent new patient starts over time'. Any initial channel stocking or a few dozen patient starts clears the revenue number. The stock will trade on whatever patient-start, enrollment or payer metric the company chooses to disclose, and no source carries a consensus for that.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior revenue print; this is the first commercial quarter. At approval (2026-09-14) the stock opened +9% pre-market and then closed -6% as traders shifted from approval risk to launch execution and pricing.
findings.why_not_priced: The revenue bar is too low to matter, so the real bar is an unpublished whisper on patient starts. The company's low-key framing on 2026-09-14 (8-K Ex 99.2) lowers the formal bar. The +15% five-day run-up suggests the whisper has moved up, which is why this is sized small and given a symmetric range.
findings.independence: 8-K Ex 99.2, 2026-09-14 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1727196/000110465926107273/tm2625362d1_ex99-2.htm): 6,600 patients, 2,600 prescribers, 140 centres, about 50/50 commercial/government payer mix, no numeric guidance. The price is from https://stocktwits.com/news-articles/markets/equity/srrk-shares-pull-back-after-fda-approval-for-genetic-disease-drug-but-wall-street-hikes-price-targets/cZtmh4bRBT3.

findings.finding: Early payer policies are narrower than the FDA label. BCBS Michigan/BCN made Isembyld prior-authorization-required effective 2026-09-28/10-01 and covers only (a) patients diagnosed with later-onset Type 2/3 SMA, (b) patients not on invasive ventilation, (c) patients with no prior gene therapy, (d) prescriptions from a pediatric-neuromuscular neurologist, and (e) patients who have tried preferred drugs (step therapy). Approval lasts 6 months, and renewal requires a documented clinically significant motor response. The label covers everyone aged 2+ on an SMN2-targeted therapy. QualChoice (CP.PHAR.737) similarly excludes prior Zolgensma/Itvisma and requires a baseline HFMSE.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no prior payer-access print. At approval the stock gave back its gains on pricing and the shift to execution (closed -6% on 2026-09-14).
findings.source_date: 2026-09-23 (PDF last modified; policy history effective 2026-09-28 and 2026-10-01)
findings.why_not_priced: Payer medical policies are not aggregated by the wire or by previews. The street read the label as 'at the broad end of expectations'. If the market had absorbed plan-level criteria that exclude Type 1 survivors and adults outside pediatric-neuromuscular practices, and that require a 6-month response, the approval-day price-target raises would have come with access caveats. This is a proxy: two regional plans out of a market split about 50/50 commercial/government. The company's comments on the call on time-to-approval and access will show whether it generalises.
findings.independence: Proxy. QualChoice criteria at https://www.qualchoice.com/media/9016/cpphar737_pepp.pdf and Blue Shield of California's PA-required policies (https://www.blueshieldca.com/content/dam/bsca/en/provider/docs/bsc-med-benefit-drug-policy/apitegromab-mstn-Isembyld-COMM-UMRx-provider.pdf) point the same way on PA friction. These are restrictions typical of a launch and are not company-confirmed.

findings.finding: The stock rose into the print with no cause I could find: $39.90 on 2026-10-16 (down 17% month to date then), $43.26 on 10-29, $45.50 on 11-05, and $49.375 sealed on 11-09 (+15% over 5 days). I found no company news, filing (other than the Form 4 above) or analyst action dated 2026-11-02 to 11-09. The run-up raises the bar for the patient-start whisper.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: At approval the stock ran up and then sold the news (-6% on 2026-09-14). The two large positive prints (+24%, +10%) came on regulatory news, not on run-ups.
findings.why_not_priced: The run-up is itself in the price. The open question is whether it reflects a raised whisper on starts that the print must now beat. An unexplained move is weak evidence either way, so this is sized near zero.

findings.finding: The EU timeline has slipped by about a year. Scholar Rock withdrew the apitegromab MAA (completed 20 Aug 2026; EMA's provisional view was that it 'could not have been authorised' because the manufacturing site had not shown EU GMP compliance in time). The company resubmitted with an alternate fill-finish site around 8 Oct 2026 and targets a CHMP opinion in 1H 2027. The Q2 release had promised guidance once aligned with the EMA; the Q3 release will restate the timeline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Regulatory-timing news moved this stock hard: -9.3% around 2026-10-14 on renewed sensitivity to manufacturing and regulatory timing, and +24% on 2025-11-14 on an FDA path.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the withdrawal and resubmission are public. The residual is whether the call confirms 1H 2027 or pushes it out, and whether a Japan decision is dated. A slip beyond 1H27 would be new.
findings.independence: Company release https://investors.scholarrock.com/news-releases/news-release-details/scholar-rock-provides-update-global-apitegromab-regulatory; the 1H 2027 CHMP target is single-sourced (https://briefglance.com/companies/scholar-rock-holding-corporation/pulses/85926).

findings.finding: Non-dilutive capital is available and may be announced with the print. On approval the company said it intends to monetise its Rare Pediatric Disease priority review voucher (recent PRV sales are around $150M) and that an additional $150M is available under its debt facility. Cash was $492.1M on 30 Jun 2026 against about $76M a quarter of operating cash burn (H1: $152.4M). I found no PRV sale announced as of 9 Nov.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Financing news on this name has been read positively when non-dilutive. The stock rose about 7% on the $550M funding package (tikr). The Q2 2026 ATM ($62.8M net) did not stop a +10% print reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The PRV sale is an intention with no date. If the market had priced a near-certain about-$150M non-dilutive inflow, dilution worries (rallies.ai cited 'dilution fears') would not have been a reason for October's slide. The money funds a corroborated launch (approved drug, about 50 field staff, supply ready), so the sign is positive or zero.
findings.independence: Q2 2026 8-K Ex 99.1 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001727196/000119312526336715/srrk-ex99_1.htm): $492.1M cash, ATM $62.8M net in Q2. https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/scholar-rock-resubmits-apitegromab-bla-for-sma-adds-second-fill-finish-site-fda-decision-eyed-by-sept-2026-03-31/: $150M debt option at approval.

findings.finding: The FDA imposed post-marketing requirements that management misstated on the approval call and corrected in a Reg FD 8-K: a pregnancy safety study, and every serious or non-serious fracture case reported as a 15-day alert report. The label carries a fracture warning. Fracture or safety commentary from the first weeks of real-world use is a downside channel on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior safety print. The correction (2026-09-15) came during the -6% post-approval fade.
findings.why_not_priced: Public since September and probably priced. The residual is only an unexpected safety signal, which I have no evidence of.
findings.independence: Fracture risk is also in the 8-K Ex 99.2 of 2026-09-14 and the FDA label (https://www.accessdata.fda.gov/drugsatfda_docs/label/2026/761463Orig1s000lbl.pdf).

findings.finding: The nearest muscle-targeted SMA rival is gone: Roche/Chugai discontinued emugrobart (GYM329) in SMA and FSHD in March 2026 after inconsistent functional efficacy in MANATEE. ISEMBYLD is the only muscle-targeted SMA therapy, which supports how management frames uptake on the call.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it has been public for eight months. The residual is that the launch has no competitive comparison and no clinical-trial competitor, which matters little for one quarter.

outside_window.finding: EU CHMP opinion on the resubmitted MAA, targeted for 1H 2027.
SRK-439 Phase 1 healthy-volunteer topline data guided for late 2026; ONYX extension primary completion is listed as 2026-11-01 on ClinicalTrials.gov, so data would come later.

baseline_tension: Mixed. The put skew (+28 vol points) and the +15% five-day run-up both argue for downside, while the crowded short (about 18% of shares outstanding, 12.7 days to cover), the director's $12M buy and the near-zero revenue bar argue for upside. The net is close to a coin flip on a large move.
lessons_applied: Rule 5 (an unexplained move is worth about 0): the run-up-with-no-cause finding shrank from -0.5 to -0.1.
Rule 7 (a crowded short shrinks negatives): the BCBSM/payer-restriction finding went from -0.6 to -0.4 and the fracture/PMR finding from -0.2 to -0.15; p_up moved from 47 to 49.
Rule 6 (disputed bar): the revenue consensus has one source with two disagreeing snapshots, so the reported-quarter finding stays capped at +0.3 and all sizes stay small; no change needed.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the PRV and debt finding funds a corroborated launch, so it stays at +0.4.
Unchanged: the director buy, the short-interest finding, the EU timeline and the competitor finding.
